# Tobit Chapter 14 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 14 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_014_page_001.jpg

---

**14:1** And Tobit ended his words of praise. He was fifty-eight years old when he lost his sight, and after eight years he recovered it; and he gave alms and continued fearing the Lord his God and giving thanks to him.

**14:2** And when he had grown very old, he called his son and the six grandsons and said to them, "My child, take your sons.

**14:3** See, I have grown old and am ready to depart from life. Go to Media, my child, for I believe all the words of Nahum the prophet concerning Nineveh — that everything will be fulfilled and will overtake Assyria and Nineveh; all that the prophets of Israel spoke, whom God sent.

**14:4** Not one of those words will fall short; everything will happen at its appointed time. And in Media it will be safer than in Assyria and Babylon. For I know and believe that everything God has spoken will be fulfilled and will come to pass, and not one word of the prophecies will fail.

**14:5** All our kindred who dwell in the land of Israel will be scattered and taken captive from the good land, and all the land of Israel will become a wasteland — and Samaria and Jerusalem will become a wasteland — and the house of God will lie in sorrow and will be burned for a time.

**14:6** "But God will again have mercy on them and bring them back to the land of Israel; and they will rebuild the house, though not as the former one, until the time when the appointed season is fulfilled. And after these things they will all return from their captivity and will rebuild Jerusalem with honor, and the house of God will be rebuilt in it, as the prophets of Israel spoke concerning it.

**14:7** And all the nations throughout the whole earth will turn and fear God in truth; all of them will abandon their idols, which have led them into error, and will bless the God of the ages in righteousness.

**14:8** All the sons of Israel who are saved in those days, remembering God in truth, will be gathered together and will come to Jerusalem and will dwell forever in the land of Abraham in safety, and it will be given over to them. And those who love God in truth will rejoice, and those who commit sin and unrighteousness will be absent from all the earth.

**14:9** "Now then, my children, I command you: serve God faithfully and do what is pleasing before him; and command your children also to do righteousness and to give alms, to be mindful of God and to bless his name at all times sincerely and with all their strength.

**14:10** Now, my child, leave Nineveh, for what Nahum said will surely come to pass. Go to Media — there it will be safe. From my youth I trusted Ahikar, and he helped me until I reached old age. Remember what he did to Nadan, his brother's son? He dragged him down into the earth, but Ahikar himself came up into the light. Ahikar gave alms and was saved from the deadly snare that Nadan had set for him; but Nadan fell into the snare of death, and it destroyed him.

**14:11** Now then, my children — see what almsgiving does, and what unrighteousness does: it kills! But now my soul is ready to depart."

**14:12** And they laid him on his bed, and he died and was buried honorably.

**14:13** And when his mother Anna died, Tobias buried her with his father. Then Tobias departed with his wife and children to Ecbatana, to his father-in-law Raguel.

**14:14** He grew old with honor, and he buried his parents-in-law with honor, and he inherited their estate and the estate of his father Tobit.

**14:15** And he died in Ecbatana of Media, being ninety-nine years old. He saw and heard of the destruction of Nineveh, which Nebuchadnezzar and Ahasuerus had captured; and before his death he rejoiced over Nineveh.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

**Age figures:** All three agents follow Codex Sinaiticus (GII): Tobit blind at 58, sight restored at 66, dies at 112 (implied); Tobias dies at 99. The note about Vaticanus figures (158, 127) is recorded in the Disagreement Log.

**Nahum vs. Jonah:** All three agents correctly follow Sinaiticus in reading Nahum. This is an important text-critical decision — some traditions harmonize to Jonah (the more famous Nineveh prophet). Sinaiticus preserves what may be the more primitive reading.

**Verse 10 — "his brother's son":** EMET has "the-man Nadan who [was] his-brother's-[son]"; LOGOS has "the son of his brother"; PNEUMA has "his nephew." Consensus follows LOGOS for precision.

**Verse 5 — "house of God":** All three agents render *oikos tou theou* as "house of God" (LOGOS, EMET) or "temple of God" (PNEUMA). Consensus uses "house of God" as the more literal and standard rendering.

**Verse 7 — "in truth":** EMET: "who-lead-astray them erroneously"; LOGOS: "which have led them into error"; PNEUMA: "that have been lying to them for generations." Consensus takes LOGOS — "led them into error" is the most accurate and avoids PNEUMA's temporal addition.

**Verse 11 — Final moral:** PNEUMA's "it kills its owner" is an expansion; the Greek has simply the contrast of almsgiving (life) vs. sin (death). Consensus returns to LOGOS.

---
## Disagreement Log

| Verse | Issue | EMET | LOGOS | PNEUMA | Resolution |
|-------|-------|------|-------|--------|------------|
| 14:1 | Tobit's life summary | "fifty-eight years [old] when he-lost his-eyesight" | "fifty-eight years old when he lost his sight" | "fifty-eight years old when he went blind" | **LOGOS** — cleanest; all agree on the Sinaiticus figure |
| 14:2 | Address to family | "the six-sons of his-son" | "the six grandsons" | "his six grandchildren" | **LOGOS** — "six grandsons" is natural; EMET's construct is literal but awkward; PNEUMA's "grandchildren" is fine but LOGOS is more precise to *tous hex huious* |
| 14:3 | "I-trust" vs. "I-believe" | "I-trust all the-words of Nahum" | "I believe all the words of Nahum" | "I believe with all my heart the words...of Nahum" | **LOGOS** — PNEUMA adds "with all my heart" which is not in the Greek |
| 14:3 | Named prophet | "Nahum" | "Nahum" | "the prophet Nahum" | All agree: **Nahum** — Sinaiticus is clear |
| 14:5 | Temple language | "house of God will-be-in-sorrow and will-be-burned" | "house of God will lie in sorrow and will be burned" | "temple of God will be left in mourning and burned" | **LOGOS** — "lie in sorrow" is a nice rendering of *lyupēthēsetai*; "in mourning" (PNEUMA) is acceptable but "temple" diverges from "house" (*oikos*) |
| 14:6 | Temporal limit | "until the-time-when the-times-of the-age are-fulfilled" | "until the time when the appointed season is fulfilled" | "not until the appointed time has been fully completed" | **LOGOS** — "appointed season" captures *ho kairos tou aiōnos* well; EMET's nested "times-of the-age" is literal but murky |
| 14:7 | Idols as deceivers | "who-lead-astray them erroneously" | "which have led them into error" | "that have been lying to them for generations" | **LOGOS** — "into error" is accurate; PNEUMA's "for generations" adds temporal scope not in source |
| 14:8 | Final eschatological exclusion | "those-who-commit sin and unrighteousness will-be-absent from all the-earth" | "those who commit sin and unrighteousness will be absent from all the earth" | "Those who choose sin and injustice will be gone from the earth entirely" | **LOGOS** — "absent from the earth" is striking; PNEUMA's "gone entirely" is a doublet |
| 14:9 | *Eleēmosyna* in moral charge | "to-do righteousness and eleēmosyna" (transliterated) | "to do righteousness and to give alms" | "do right, give to those in need" | **LOGOS** — "give alms" is the standard English for *eleēmosyna*; EMET's transliteration is scholarly but disrupts; PNEUMA loses the technical term |
| 14:10 | Nadan's relationship | "the-man Nadan who [was] his-brother's-[son]" | "Nadan, his brother's son" | "his nephew Nadan" | **LOGOS** — "his brother's son" is more precise than "nephew" (avoids ambiguity of the Ahikar tradition) |
| 14:10 | Ahikar's deliverance mechanism | "Ahikar gave eleēmosyna and escaped the-death-trap" | "Ahikar gave alms and was saved from the deadly snare" | "It was his generosity that saved him" | **LOGOS** — "deadly snare" is vivid and accurate; PNEUMA paraphrases away the "snare" (*pagis*) image |
| 14:11 | Final moral formulation | "see what eleēmosyna does...but Nadan fell-into the-trap" | "see what almsgiving does...it kills!" | "See what generosity does. See what wickedness does: it kills its owner" | **LOGOS** — preserves the structural contrast; PNEUMA's "kills its owner" adds "its owner" not in the Greek |
| 14:14 | Tobias's final status | "he-grew-old honorably" | "He grew old with honor" | "He grew old with grace and dignity" | **LOGOS** — "with honor" is most faithful to *meta timēs*; PNEUMA's "grace and dignity" doubles the concept |
| 14:15 | Tobias's witness of Nineveh | "he-saw and he-heard of the-destruction" | "He saw and heard of the destruction" | "He lived long enough to hear the news" | **LOGOS/EMET** — PNEUMA drops "saw" (*eiden*); the Greek explicitly has both seeing and hearing |
